introduction: Bram has caught you at the fence line the evening before the Public Farm. He calls it a courtesy. You have one question to put to him before he waddles off.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Attacking the animal instead of the argument. How long Rue has been here is not a fact about the water.
Treating a crowd as a reason. Forty-one animals agreeing is not forty-one animals having checked.

sentences.text: Rue — a courtesy, before Sunday. The Flock is putting the motion regardless.
Forty-one birds have already said yes, and forty-one is not a mistake.

logicalFallacies.explanation: The number of birds who said yes is offered as the reason the motion is right. None of them is said to have looked at the water.

sentences.text: You'd be arguing against the whole pond, and you've been on this farm six weeks.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Six weeks is a fact about Rue, not about the pond. It is used to retire his objection without answering it.

options.reason: You answered a crowd with a smaller crowd. Now the argument is about how many animals are on each side, which is the one contest you cannot win.

sentences.text: Every donkey on this farm thinks the grate is the problem — that's four of us, and we're the ones who carry the water.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Counting donkeys is the same move Bram just made, only with a worse number. Whether the grate is the problem does not depend on who agrees.

options.reason: A fair question about the arithmetic, but it accepts that the vote count is what settles the pond. Bram is happy to argue about numbers all evening.

sentences.text: Is forty-one a majority, though? How many animals are on this farm altogether?

options.reason: Names both moves — the crowd and the newcomer jab — as things that are not about the water, then offers a check anyone can run. Bram concedes the grate on the record.

unlockedSentences.text: You said forty-one agreed, and that I've only been here six weeks. Neither of those is about the water. So let's do the one that is: come to the outflow with me now, and if the grate isn't bent, I'll drop it before Sunday.

sentences.text: Four donkeys against forty-one birds. Thank you, Rue. You've just made my argument for me.
More than forty-one, I expect. But they didn't turn up, did they.
…It's bent. It's been bent since before the frost. That doesn't mean the hooves aren't also — look. Take it up with Duchess on Sunday.
Sunday, then. Tobias has the motion. Duchess speaks first.
And Rue — she's much better at this than I am.
